<!-- Page: Quickstart (https://work.hogman.network/docs/) -->

# Quickstart

Take equipment controllers and internal web tools off the open internet in four steps — reachable by authorized staff in ordinary browsers over standard HTTPS, with zero public IP addresses.

## 1. Plan pens by site or region

Before creating your first pen, decide how to group locations. For multi-site businesses, create a separate pen per region or store group (for example, `region-north` and `region-south`, or `store-north`) rather than putting every location in one shared network. Separate pens limit blast radius if a laptop is lost or an account is compromised.

## 2. Create a pen

Request access or create your pen at [get.hogman.network](https://get.hogman.network/#wait#wait) and claim a neutral name for your network (for example, `store-north`). Hogman spins up an isolated private DNS zone (`store-north.pens.hogman.network`) and a web management portal where owners and admins control access.

When setup finishes, the sign-up page gives you your first single-use join link.

## 3. Join a workstation and bridge an internal service

Open your join link on a Mac or Linux computer and run the short command it displays in Terminal:

```text
$ curl -fsSL https://store-north.gate.hogman.network/start | sh
```

The script prompts for your invite link, verifies `hogman-join` against its published SHA-256 checksum, saves it to `~/hogman-join`, and connects your browser to the pen. Ordinary internet browsing stays untouched.

Next, close any public router port-forwarding pointing at your internal device or web app, then bridge its local web interface into the pen:

```text
$ ~/hogman-join share cooler-1 http://192.168.1.40 --background

✓ https://cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network is up.
  Everyone in the pen can open it.
```

The local upstream can speak plain HTTP on your LAN while staff always connect over standard HTTPS (port 443) with a publicly trusted Let's Encrypt certificate and zero open firewall ports. For headless Raspberry Pi or mini PC site bridges, see [Bridging equipment & apps](https://work.hogman.network/docs/share.html).

## 4. Onboard staff and appoint a second owner

Open your pen's management portal (`https://home.<yourpen>.pens.hogman.network`) to create single-use invite links for employees and outside contractors, suspend temporary access, or offboard someone from every device in ~2 seconds.

**Appoint a backup owner right away:** Hogman has zero account recovery and no support backdoor. If a pen's only owner loses every enrolled device, nobody can administer that pen again. Promote a second trusted owner under *Members* as soon as they join.

Full details: [Onboarding staff & devices](https://work.hogman.network/docs/join.html) and [Managing access & offboarding](https://work.hogman.network/docs/keeper.html).

## Going deeper
  [**Architecture & security** Packet flow, WireGuard + TLS 1.3, split-horizon DNS-01, threat model, and SLSA verification.](https://work.hogman.network/docs/security.html) [**FAQ & troubleshooting** Firmware boundaries, multi-site design, contractor access, corporate VPNs, and common fixes.](https://work.hogman.network/docs/faq.html)

<!-- Page: Onboarding staff & devices (https://work.hogman.network/docs/join.html) -->

# Onboarding staff & devices

How employees and contractors connect a Mac or Linux laptop to a pen using a single-use invite link — without routing ordinary browsing through a VPN.

## Connecting a first workstation

1. **Open the invite link** on the workstation that needs access. Invite links work once and expire after 7 days.
2. **Run the setup command** shown on the page in Terminal — it is the same short command for everyone in the pen:

```text
$ curl -fsSL https://store-north.gate.hogman.network/start | sh
```
 The script prompts for the invite link (use the page's *Copy my invite link* button), downloads `hogman-join` for the platform, verifies its published SHA-256 checksum, saves it as `~/hogman-join`, and runs it. The invite token never appears in shell arguments or history. [Inspect the script](https://github.com/celtiberi/hogman/blob/main/core/join-page/start.sh) first, or expand the manual download steps on the join page.
3. **Choose a handle** when prompted (lowercase letters, digits, and dashes, 2–32 characters — for example, `alex-ops`).
4. **Confirm access.** `hogman-join` verifies the gate against the operating system's built-in HTTPS trust store, confirms the pen portal loads over HTTPS, configures the browser proxy, and opens it. Keep `~/hogman-join` on the machine for updates, hosting, and disconnecting later.

**Expected macOS prompts during first setup:**

- **"Allow hogman-join to find devices on local networks?"** Either choice works. *Allow* lets devices on the same LAN connect directly over WireGuard; *Don't Allow* routes encrypted traffic through the relay instead. Nothing on the local LAN is exposed either way.
- **Your Mac's password**, once, to configure the system automatic proxy URL so browsers resolve pen hostnames. If skipped, `hogman-join` prints the PAC URL to configure manually.

**If setup is interrupted partway** (offline or DNS still propagating), resolve the issue and run the same command again. If it stopped before redeeming the invite, the link remains unused; if after, the rerun detects the enrolled workstation and finishes setup.

## Manual downloads

For environments where IT stages binaries directly, platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` are hosted under `/join/dl/` on the pen's gate host:
| Platform | Binary |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hogman-join-Darwin-arm64` |
| macOS, Intel | `hogman-join-Darwin-x86_64` |
| Linux, x86-64 | `hogman-join-Linux-x86_64` |
| Linux, ARM64 (Raspberry Pi 4/5, ARM servers) | `hogman-join-Linux-aarch64` |
| Windows (built, untested) | `hogman-join-windows-amd64.exe` |

## Using alongside a corporate VPN

On macOS, Network Extension VPN clients (corporate VPNs, WireGuard, ProtonVPN, Mullvad) override the system automatic proxy setting while connected, so browsers stop resolving pen hostnames even though `hogman-join` stays connected.

- **Firefox (works today, no extension required):** set Firefox's built-in *Settings → Network Settings → Automatic proxy configuration URL* to the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/proxy.pac` URL printed by `hogman-join`. Pen hostnames route through `hogman-join` while ordinary browsing stays on the VPN.
- **Chrome, Brave, Edge, and Firefox extension (developer preview):** the companion extension in `browser-ext/` is not yet published on the Chrome Web Store or Mozilla Add-ons. Teams can load it manually from `browser-ext/dist/` (see `browser-ext/README.md`; note that Firefox removes temporary add-ons on restart, and Firefox Private Windows send pen names to public DNS unless *Run in Private Windows* is enabled for the extension).
- **Safari:** Apple does not expose proxy APIs to Safari extensions, so pause the VPN while accessing pen dashboards in Safari.

## How the client connects

`hogman-join` runs a small unprivileged userspace process as the logged-in user (no `TUN` interface, no root daemon) that starts at login. It carries **HTTPS (port 443) to pen servers and nothing else** (plain `http://` requests redirect locally to HTTPS). Regular internet browsing, local LAN access, and any existing Tailscale installation remain untouched. See [what Hogman deliberately does not do](https://work.hogman.network/docs/faq.html#not).

## Browsers and command-line tools

Only applications configured to use the pen's loopback proxy (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:21234`) can reach pen sites:

- **Browsers:** on macOS, `hogman-join` sets the automatic proxy URL (never overwriting an existing non-Hogman proxy). Joining multiple site pens updates one combined `proxy.pac` automatically. On Linux, point the browser or desktop automatic proxy setting to the printed `proxy.pac` URL (one URL covers all joined pens; reload proxy settings after joining or leaving a pen).
- **curl (per command):**

```text
$ https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:21234 curl https://cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network
```
 Do not export `https_proxy` globally in your shell — the proxy refuses all non-pen hostnames.
- **git (per host):**

```text
$ git config --global http.https://git.store-north.pens.hogman.network/.proxy http://127.0.0.1:21234
```

## Adding a second workstation

From the pen's portal, press **Add a device** to generate a single-use link and QR code (valid for 1 hour). Open it on the second laptop and run the setup command; it enrolls under the same member account. Mobile support is in progress.

For an always-on on-site bridge or server, do not use a personal device link — use a share link as documented in [Bridging equipment & apps](https://work.hogman.network/docs/share.html).

## Updating and disconnecting

```text
$ ~/hogman-join update
```

Fetches the latest binary from the pen's gate (or a specified host), verifies its SHA-256 against `SHA256SUMS` over HTTPS, restarts the background agent and service-managed bridges, and cleans up legacy state. Pass `--pen ZONE` when connected to multiple pens, or `--dry-run` to preview.

```text
$ ~/hogman-join leave '<your pen link or zone>'
```

Stops any bridges running on that machine, shuts down the background connection, and clears its proxy configuration. Membership remains active — owners and admins remove accounts from the portal.

## CLI options

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--handle NAME` | Set the member handle without interactive prompting. |
| `--hostname NAME` | Override the enrolled device label (default: computer hostname). |
| `--no-service` | Run in the background without installing a login service. |
| `--no-system-proxy` | Skip modifying the macOS system automatic proxy setting. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate the link and pen without making changes. |
| `--no-open` | Do not launch a browser when finished (useful on headless Linux). |
| `--pen ZONE` | Target a specific pen for `share` or `update`. |

Run `~/hogman-join --help` for the complete flag list.

<!-- Page: Bridging equipment & apps (https://work.hogman.network/docs/share.html) -->

# Bridging equipment & apps

Keep refrigeration controllers, HVAC/BMS panels, cameras, and internal web apps strictly on your local network, and bridge only their web interfaces into a pen over standard HTTPS (port 443).

```text
$ ~/hogman-join share cooler-1 http://192.168.1.40 --background

• Adding a server for cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network (ops-north)
• Proxying http://192.168.1.40 as https://cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network

✓ https://cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network is up.
  Everyone in the pen can open it.
  Take it down and free the name: hogman-join share stop cooler-1
```

## What you can bridge

| Target | Command | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **On-site LAN equipment** | `share cooler-1 http://192.168.1.40` | Bridges a local controller, HVAC/BMS panel, camera NVR, or NAS web UI into the pen over HTTPS with zero open router ports. The local device can speak plain HTTP while staff always connect over HTTPS (`:443`). |
| **Internal web application** | `share inventory 8080` | Reverse-proxies `http://127.0.0.1:8080` over HTTPS (WebSockets supported; forwards `X-Forwarded-For`, `-Host`, and `-Proto` while preserving the upstream `Host` header). |
| **Static manuals or reports** | `share sops ~/site-manuals` | Serves `index.html` (or a directory listing) over HTTPS inside Go's `os.Root` sandbox with no symlink escape. |

Already running Caddy or nginx on site with multiple internal apps behind it? Bridge its local port (`share ops 8080`) and let Hogman handle the private hostname and TLS.

## Dedicated on-site bridge setup

Equipment controllers cannot install client software themselves. Keep them on your local LAN and place a small always-on Linux or Mac computer (such as a Raspberry Pi 4/5 or mini PC) on the same network. The bridge machine does **not** need to enroll as a personal member device:

1. **Close public router ports:** remove any public IP mapping or router port-forwarding pointing at the controller. Verify its web panel answers only on the local LAN (for example, `http://192.168.1.40`).
2. **Generate a share link:** on your pen's management portal, press **Get a share link** and copy the single-use server link (valid for 1 hour). Always use a *share link* for bridges and servers — not a member invite link.
3. **Start the bridge in the background:** download `hogman-join` on the bridge box (Raspberry Pi 4/5 uses `hogman-join-Linux-aarch64`) and pass the share link with `--background`:

```text
$ ./hogman-join share cooler-1 http://192.168.1.40 'https://store-north.gate.hogman.network/join#k=…' --background
```

4. **Enable boot startup on headless Linux:** on macOS (launchd) and Linux (systemd user services), `--background` installs a login service automatically. On a headless Linux bridge where nobody logs in after a power cycle, run once:

```text
$ sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER
```
 Pass `--no-service` only if you want a temporary background process until reboot. (Windows is built but untested and does not yet register a reboot service.)

You can run multiple `share` commands from the same on-site bridge machine — for example, one for `cooler-1` and one for `hvac-main` — and each gets its own isolated server identity and hostname. Nothing else on your LAN is exposed.

## Multi-site separation and naming

- **Separate pens per site or region:** put distinct store groups or facilities in separate pens (e.g. `region-north.pens.hogman.network` and `region-south.pens.hogman.network`) so a lost laptop or contractor account only ever reaches the locations it is assigned to.
- **Use neutral, non-sensitive hostnames:** standard public HTTPS certificates mean issued hostnames appear in public Certificate Transparency logs (names only — traffic and site contents never leave the encrypted mesh). Prefer generic operational names like `cooler-1` or `panel-b2` instead of customer names, street addresses, or sensitive model numbers.
- **Naming rules & rollback:** each share name is a single label (lowercase letters, digits, dashes) becoming `https://NAME.<pen>.pens.hogman.network`. First come, first served; up to 50 names per member. If a brand-new share fails to obtain its first certificate, it tears down its server node and releases the name automatically.

**Operational security checklist — what a bridge does and does not cover:**

- **Keep vendor firmware updates enabled:** a pen removes equipment from the public internet and restricts reachability to invited members, but **it does not patch firmware vulnerabilities**.
- **Change default device passwords:** pen membership is a strong network perimeter, not a substitute for changing factory credentials on controllers.
- **Web interfaces only (HTTPS :443):** devices that only speak raw non-HTTP protocols (such as raw Modbus, BACnet, RDP, or SSH) without a web UI are not a fit.
- **Isolated server nodes:** every share runs its own embedded `tsnet` server identity (`tag:server`) with its own local CertMagic TLS keypair. Staff laptops accept zero inbound connections, and your bridge opens zero inbound firewall ports.

## Listing and taking down bridges

```text
$ ~/hogman-join share list
https://cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network   http://192.168.1.40  (running in the background)

$ ~/hogman-join share stop cooler-1
✓ https://cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network is down, and the name is free again.
```

`share stop` shuts down that server node and releases the hostname. Disconnecting a machine with `leave` stops all shares running on it first. Connected to more than one pen? Pass `--pen <zone>`.

---

<!-- Page: Managing access & offboarding (https://work.hogman.network/docs/keeper.html) -->

# Managing access & offboarding

For pen owners and admins. Manage staff, outside contractors, invites, and active bridges from your pen's management portal at `https://home.<yourpen>.pens.hogman.network`.

## Roles and permissions

| Role | Permissions |
| --- | --- |
| **Owner** | Full administrative control. Cannot be suspended or removed. Every operational pen should have **at least two owners**: if one owner loses every enrolled device, only another owner can invite them back. Owners can demote one another, so grant Owner only to fully trusted principals. |
| **Admin** | Create and revoke invites; suspend, resume, and remove regular members. Cannot modify owners or other admins. |
| **Member** | Enroll personal workstations and register HTTPS bridges or internal apps. Creating invites is restricted to owners and admins unless explicitly enabled for members. |

## Inviting staff and contractors

Under **Invite someone**, add a short tracking note (for example, *"Jordan — refrigeration contractor, Store North"*) and press **Make an invite**. The portal generates a single-use link and QR code valid for 7 days. Treat every invite link like a physical key — whoever opens it first enrolls.

Unused links appear under **Open invites** and can be revoked at any time before redemption.

## Suspending and offboarding (~2 seconds)

The **Members** directory lists every enrolled person with their role, status, and device count (paginated with search):

- **Suspend (~2 s):** immediately cuts off all of a person's devices while keeping their account, device slots, and site names intact. Ideal for outside service vendors between work orders or temporary leave.
- **Resume (<1 s):** restores access immediately when a contractor or employee needs access again.
- **Remove (~2 s):** ends membership, deletes every device from the mesh, revokes unused keys and invites, rewrites ACLs, and **permanently retires their handle and site names** so nobody can impersonate them later. Re-entry requires a new invite.
- **Promote / demote:** grant or revoke Admin access on a member, or promote an Admin to Owner (owner-only).

**Zero account recovery — appoint a second owner:** there is no support backdoor or password reset. If someone loses every enrolled device, issue a new invite, restore their role, and remove the old account (demote an old owner to Admin first). Always keep at least two owners on every production pen.

## Devices and active services

Each member manages their own devices from the portal: **Add a device** creates a 1-hour personal join link for a second laptop, and **Get a share link** creates a 1-hour server link for an on-site bridge or always-on host ([Bridging equipment & apps](https://work.hogman.network/docs/share.html)). Active dashboards and bridged controllers appear under **Sites in this pen** with their owner and optional note.

## Audit visibility and privacy boundaries

Owners and admins can see who belongs to the pen, their enrolled devices, online status, and which pen hostnames are queried. Neither pen owners nor Hogman's control plane can passively read application traffic (WireGuard + TLS 1.3 end to end) or any browsing outside the pen. Remind staff that bridged hostnames appear in public Certificate Transparency logs (names only, never contents) and to use a separate browser profile for any pen they do not fully trust. See the full [threat model](https://work.hogman.network/docs/security.html#threat-model).

---

<!-- Page: Architecture & security (https://work.hogman.network/docs/security.html) -->

# Architecture & security

How packets move across a pen, what runs on your machine and our host, how public HTTPS works without public IPs, and the exact limits we haven't closed yet.

## Packet flow & trust boundaries

Hogman separates the **data plane** (traffic between members and shares) from the **control plane** (device keys, ACL policy, and pen DNS). Only the control plane's front door and relay ports listen on the public internet.

```text
Data plane (member browser to a share — control server sees ciphertext only)

  Browser
    │  PAC sends *.<pen>.pens.hogman.network to 127.0.0.1:<port>;
    │  all other traffic goes directly to the internet as usual
    ▼
  hogman-join  (unprivileged Go binary, userspace tsnet — blind TCP :443 CONNECT tunnel)
    │  1. Queries pen DNS (port 53 inside mesh) -> random CGNAT 100.x / fd7a:: address
    │  2. Verifies resolved IP is an enrolled peer via tsnet WhoIs (never dials LAN/127.0.0.1)
    │  3. Enforces :443 only (D-11)
    ▼
  [ WireGuard E2E encrypted tunnel + inner TLS 1.3 ]   (direct UDP, or DERP relay ciphertext)
    ▼
  hogman-join share  (separate tsnet server node, local CertMagic keypair)
    │  Reverse-proxies localhost:<port> or serves static dir via Go os.Root (no symlink escape)
    ▼
  Your web app or static site

Control plane & certificate issuance (metadata visible; no application payloads)

  *.gate.hogman.network  -->  Shared Caddy front door (strict path allowlist + TLS wildcard)
                                │
                                ▼
                        Per-pen container network (pen-<name>-core, 4 containers)
                          ├── Headscale   (random 100.64.0.0/10 IPs, WireGuard keys, ACL grants)
                          ├── core-mesh   (Tailscale node terminating mesh DNS & portal IP)
                          ├── Registrar   (Go ledger, pen DNS :53, Unix socket API to portal)
                          └── Portal      (home.<zone> Caddy + CertMagic local key)

  ns1.hogman.network     -->  Authoritative miekg/dns server (:53 UDP/TCP)
                                Serves ONLY _acme-challenge.* TXT, SOA, NS, CAA (no A/AAAA under pens.)
```

The local proxy inside `hogman-join` is a **blind TCP `CONNECT` tunnel**. It forwards encrypted TLS bytes straight between your browser and the share without terminating, inspecting, or re-signing TLS.

## Pen components & default-deny policy

Each hosted pen runs four isolated containers (~75 MB total memory) on its own Docker bridge network, with pinned versions in [core/compose.yaml](https://github.com/celtiberi/hogman/blob/main/core/compose.yaml):
| Component | Software | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Control & relay** | Headscalehttps://github.com/juanfont/headscale | Registers devices, distributes WireGuard keys, pushes ACLs and mesh DNS, and relays encrypted WireGuard ciphertext when NAT blocks direct UDP. |
| **Registrar** | Hogman (Go) | Ledger for members, roles, invites, devices, names, and audit logs. Rebuilds Headscale ACLs, serves mesh DNS, manages `home.<zone>` certs, gates share DNS-01 TXT writes, and serves the portal API over a Unix socket. |
| **Portal** | Caddyhttps://caddyserver.com | Serves `home.<pen>.pens.hogman.network` inside the mesh only. |
| **Mesh anchor** | Tailscale client | Terminates the pen's internal DNS and portal IP inside the mesh. |

Access policy is **default deny** and targets explicit device IPs (not self-asserted tags), rebuilt within ~2 s on membership changes (measured: suspend 2.0 s, resume 0.8 s, kick 2.1 s):
| Device type | Accepts inbound from | Can dial outbound to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Personal** (laptop/desktop) | Nobody | Pen DNS & portal; `tag:server` shares on `:443` only |
| **Server** (`hogman-join share`) | Active members on `:443` only | Pen services; other servers on `:443` |
| **Unenrolled / suspended** | Nobody | Nothing |

## Client isolation (`hogman-join`)

Joining a pen runs one unprivileged static Go binary embedding Tailscale's userspace `tsnet` stack:

- **No kernel interface, no root daemon:** creates no `TUN` device, edits no `/etc/hosts` or system DNS resolvers, runs as your user, and leaves existing Tailscale installs untouched. On macOS it asks for your password once only if configuring the system automatic proxy URL (not needed with the browser extension or manual browser proxy).
- **Standard OS trust store (D-18):** browsers validate pen certificates with your normal OS/browser roots. Nothing is injected into your root store, so no pen can ever sign for outside sites.
- **PAC-scoped loopback proxy:** binds to `127.0.0.1:<port>` and serves a `/proxy.pac` matching only joined pen zones. `/status` and `/proxy.pac` reject non-loopback `Host` headers (blocking DNS-rebinding reads). Plain `http://` pen URLs get an immediate local `308` redirect to HTTPS.
- **`WhoIs`-pinned dialing:** before dialing any resolved IP, `hogman-join` verifies it falls inside `100.64.0.0/10` or `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48` and that `lc.WhoIs` confirms an enrolled peer in that pen — preventing DNS rebinding to `127.0.0.1`, LAN routers, or another tailnet.
- **Personal devices stay unreachable:** personal nodes accept zero inbound connections. Shares run as separate `tag:server` nodes using dedicated `for=share` tokens, and static folder shares confine file access inside Go's `os.Root` (refusing symlink escapes).

## Encryption & split-horizon DNS-01 HTTPS

Every request to a share is encrypted twice, with keys held by the two endpoints:

1. **Outer WireGuard tunnel:** direct peer-to-peer WireGuard encrypted end to end (or ciphertext over the pen's DERP relay when NAT blocks direct UDP).
2. **Inner TLS 1.3 with standard web certificates:** each share generates its own local keypair via embedded [CertMagic](https://github.com/caddyserver/certmagic). Private TLS keys never leave the server machine.

Publicly trusted certificates on private `100.x` IPs work via **split-horizon DNS-01**:

- **Zero public addresses:** `ns1.hogman.network` (authoritative `miekg/dns`) serves only `SOA`, `NS`, `CAA`, and 10-minute `_acme-challenge.*` `TXT` records (max 2 live per name). Every other query under `pens.hogman.network` returns empty `NODATA`.
- **Ownership enforcement & caps:** shares call the registrar over the mesh (`POST /api/acme/txt`). The registrar checks live mesh identity, enforces `serverMayUse` (a share can only certify names pointing solely to itself), and writes challenges using the pen's scoped hashed API token (capped at 5 distinct new names/hour and 20/7 days per pen, plus a 40/hour soft / 60/hour hard global ceiling across all pens that reserves headroom for quiet and newly created pens; attempts count, not issued certs, and a name already counted in the last 7 days (retries) is free).
- **CAA + CA failover:** `pens.hogman.network` publishes strict `dns-01` CAA rules for `letsencrypt.org` (primary, with ARI) and `pki.goog` (Google Trust Services failover via single-use mesh EAB on 429/5xx, with persistent backoff up to 1 h). Hosted gates share a wildcard `*.gate.hogman.network` cert so pen names stay out of gate CT entries.

**Public-certificate trade-offs:**

- **Certificate Transparency (RFC 6962):** pen and site hostnames (e.g. `cooler-1.store-north.pens.hogman.network`) appear in public CT logs when certificates are issued. Site contents and traffic never leave the mesh.
- **Cookie/same-site scope until PSL listing (D-19):** until `pens.hogman.network` joins the Public Suffix List, browsers treat hosted pens as sibling subdomains for cookies. Use a separate browser profile for any pen you don't fully trust.

## Threat model & trust boundaries

Hogman is private, not anonymous. Here is what each party can see or do, and what stops them:
| Adversary | Can see or try | What stops them |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive ISP, Wi-Fi, or internet scanner | WireGuard UDP / DERP ciphertext to relay IP, plus public CT hostnames. Cannot resolve pen `A`/`AAAA` records or probe mesh ports. | Zero public addresses under `pens.`, strict front-door path allowlist, end-to-end WireGuard + inner TLS 1.3. |
| Compromised DERP relay or front-door proxy | WireGuard public keys, packet timing/sizes, and front-door control HTTP traffic. | Relay never holds WireGuard private keys or share TLS private keys. |
| Malicious member inside your pen | Valid mesh identity and ability to resolve share names in the pen. | Headscale ACL allows `:443` toward `tag:server` only (no SSH, no lateral traffic, no exit nodes). `serverMayUse` blocks name/cert hijacking. Keepers can suspend or kick in ~2 s; kicked site names are retired permanently. |
| Hostile pen targeting your laptop | Controls that pen's DNS replies, Headscale map, and invite payload. | Unprivileged binary (no `TUN`/root daemon), no OS root CA, client-side zone validation, loopback `Host` checks, `WhoIs` dial pin, and `:443`-only proxy gate. |
| Compromised keeper or hosting server (control plane) | **Sees:** member list, device keys/IPs, online times, mesh DNS lookups. **Could try:** enrolling a rogue device, rewriting ACLs, or writing a DNS-01 challenge TXT record. | Cannot passively read WireGuard payloads or share TLS private keys. Any rogue certificate minted via DNS-01 must appear in public CT logs (no silent MITM). Support cannot recover accounts (D-16). |

## Host isolation & supply chain

- **Hosted control plane (D-24), open source (AGPL-3.0):** every pen runs in its own isolated Docker bridge (`pen-<name>-core`) with its own SQLite database, Headscale instance, keys, and UDP relay port.
- **Container & host hardening:** pen containers and the shared Caddy front door run non-root (`uid 65532`), read-only (`tmpfs` for `/tmp`), with `cap_drop: [ALL]` and `no-new-privileges`. The front door enforces an explicit Headscale path allowlist plus HSTS, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP, `nosniff`, and `Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?1`.
- **Service isolation:** the registrar's internal HTTP API listens only on a kernel-enforced Unix domain socket shared with the portal, verifies `X-Forwarded-For` against live Headscale nodes, and enforces strict CSRF checks. `challenge-dns` and `gate-cert` run under dedicated unprivileged systemd sandboxes (`ProtectSystem=strict`, syscall filters, `LoadCredential`). Used pen names are burned permanently (D-21).
- **Verifiable CI-only builds:** public DNS changes go through reviewed PRs with `dnscontrol preview` (D-23). Release binaries are built exclusively in GitHub Actions with SLSA build provenance — verify any download yourself:

```text
$ gh attestation verify hogman-join --repo celtiberi/hogman
```

Full self-audit (OWASP ASVS, CIS Docker/Linux, SLSA): [audit-2026-11.md](https://github.com/celtiberi/hogman/blob/main/docs/security/audit-2026-11.md) · PKI architecture note: [public-certificates.md](https://github.com/celtiberi/hogman/blob/main/docs/security/public-certificates.md).

## Known limits & deliberate omissions

- **Not independently audited yet:** reviewed internally against standard checklists, not yet tested by an external security firm.
- **Device keys on disk:** pen credentials currently live in user-readable state files rather than hardware/TPM/Keychain binding; copying those files lets someone use that device slot until removed.
- **Auto-update verification:** `hogman-join update` checks HTTPS transport and published `SHA256SUMS` rather than a key pinned inside the binary (signed updates planned).
- **Public Suffix List (D-19):** `pens.hogman.network` is not yet on the PSL, so use separate browser profiles across mutually untrusted pens. The optional browser extension enforces allowlist-by-default per profile.
- **Optional browser extension (developer preview):** the companion extension in `browser-ext/` (for VPN coexistence on Chrome, Brave, Edge, and Firefox) is not yet published to the Chrome Web Store or Mozilla Add-ons. Once published, store installs will trust store auto-updates and our publisher account for browser proxy rules. To minimize blast radius, it has zero third-party dependencies, requests no `<all_urls>` or page-reading permissions, fails closed for `*.pens.hogman.network` (except when another non-Hogman OS proxy is active and not overridden, in which case it steps aside so your OS proxy keeps working and pen names follow that OS proxy until overridden), builds reproducibly from `browser-ext/`, and speaks to a read-only native host (`hogman-native-host`) returning only verified pen zones and loopback ports.
- **HTTPS to servers only (D-11):** no SSH, arbitrary UDP/TCP, member-to-member connections, exit nodes, or LAN subnet routing — omitted by design.

---

<!-- Page: FAQ & troubleshooting (https://work.hogman.network/docs/faq.html) -->

# FAQ & troubleshooting

Direct answers to operational, security, and deployment questions, plus fixes for common client and bridge errors.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a Hogman pen patch vulnerabilities in our equipment?

No. A pen removes equipment controllers and internal dashboards from the open internet and restricts reachability to invited pen members, which eliminates drive-by scanning and external opportunistic attacks. **It does not patch device firmware or fix bugs inside web apps.** Keep vendor security updates enabled and replace default device passwords.

### Can an equipment controller that can't install software join a pen?

Yes — keep the controller strictly on your local LAN with no router port-forwarding, and run `hogman-join share` on a small always-on Linux or Mac computer (such as a Raspberry Pi or mini PC) on the same local network. The local upstream can speak plain HTTP while staff always connect over standard HTTPS (`:443`). See [Dedicated on-site bridge setup](https://work.hogman.network/docs/share.html#bridge).

### Should all of our locations share one pen?

For multi-site operations, no. Create a separate pen per region or store group (for example, `region-north` and `region-south`) so a single lost laptop or compromised contractor account cannot reach every facility.

### How should we manage outside contractors and service vendors?

Create a single-use invite link in the specific site pen they service and tag it with their name and work order. When the visit ends, press **Suspend** (~2 s, reversible for recurring vendors) or **Remove** (~2 s, permanent, retires their handle and site names). See [Suspending and offboarding](https://work.hogman.network/docs/keeper.html#members).

### Why not just use a corporate VPN or Tailscale?

Traditional VPNs route ordinary browsing through a central gateway and often expose whole LAN subnets by default. Tailscale is excellent for personal and engineering meshes — Hogman is built on Tailscale's open-source `tsnet` and runs cleanly alongside it. Hogman is purpose-built for small teams and operations that need zero-IT browser access to specific web panels: single-use invite links, HTTPS-only (`:443`) to explicitly shared servers, standard public HTTPS certificates without a custom root CA, and a built-in web portal for ~2 s revocation.

### Can we self-host a Hogman pen control plane?

Hogman runs pen control planes hosted-only on `hogman.network` (we do not support self-hosted pen servers or custom pen domains). Your equipment, bridges, and internal web apps stay on your own machines over end-to-end encrypted WireGuard. The entire codebase is AGPL-3.0 on [GitHub](https://github.com/celtiberi/hogman) with SLSA-attested releases (`gh attestation verify hogman-join --repo celtiberi/hogman`), and teams can read the [operator guide](https://github.com/celtiberi/hogman/blob/main/deploy/README.md) to inspect how the hosted platform runs.

### What does Hogman deliberately not do?

Anything other than HTTPS (port 443) to explicitly shared server nodes. There is no SSH, no raw TCP/UDP (such as raw Modbus, BACnet, or RDP without a web UI), no exit nodes, no LAN subnet routing, and zero inbound connections to staff laptops. Every extra protocol expands attack surface on employee machines, so there is no toggle to enable them.

### Can internet scanners, bots, or AI crawlers find our bridged devices?

No. Pen hostnames have zero public `A`/`AAAA` records (`ns1.hogman.network` returns empty `NODATA` except for temporary ACME challenge tokens), and mesh IPs are not routable from the public internet. Hogman adds zero ads, trackers, or analytics anywhere. What a pen cannot prevent: an authorized user screenshotting or exporting data, an internal app phoning home on its own, or site hostnames appearing in public Certificate Transparency logs (names only — never site contents or IPs).

### Can Hogman or a pen owner read our internal traffic?

Not passively. Traffic between staff browsers and bridged servers is encrypted end to end with WireGuard + inner TLS 1.3. Owners and the hosted control plane can see membership, enrolled devices, and mesh DNS lookups, and control admission/DNS-01 — see the full [threat model](https://work.hogman.network/docs/security.html#threat-model).

### Can a manager belong to multiple site pens?

Yes — join each site pen with its own invite link. Local proxies run side by side and share one combined `proxy.pac`. Until `pens.hogman.network` is listed on the Public Suffix List, use a separate browser profile for any pen you do not fully trust so cookies remain isolated.

### What if an employee loses a laptop?

An owner or admin should immediately suspend or remove the account (or the employee can remove the lost laptop under *Your devices* from another enrolled workstation) — pen credentials live in user-readable state files on disk. If someone loses **every** enrolled device, **there is no account recovery** and no support backdoor: issue a fresh invite, restore their role, and remove the old account. **Always appoint a second owner on every production pen.**

### Platform support, pricing, and security audit status?

Hogman is currently an invite-only testbed while commercial plans are prepared. macOS and Linux work today; Windows is built but untested, and mobile apps are in progress. The software is open source (AGPL-3.0) and has **not yet had an independent security audit** — evaluate carefully before relying on it for safety-critical systems.

## Troubleshooting

### Pen dashboards say "DNS address could not be found" while a corporate VPN is active

On macOS, Network Extension VPNs (corporate VPNs, WireGuard, ProtonVPN, Mullvad) override the system automatic proxy setting while connected, causing browsers to fall back to public DNS — where pen hostnames intentionally do not exist. The `hogman-join` connection is still up. Pause the VPN while checking pen dashboards, or set Firefox's built-in *Automatic proxy configuration URL* to the address printed by `hogman-join` so pen names route to `hogman-join` while ordinary traffic stays on the VPN. (A companion browser extension for Chrome, Brave, Edge, and Firefox is in `browser-ext/` for manual developer install while store listings are prepared.)

### The browser can't find pen sites (no VPN running)

Only applications using the pen's local proxy can resolve pen names. On macOS, `hogman-join` sets the automatic proxy URL automatically unless another non-Hogman proxy is already configured (in which case it prints the URL to set manually). On Linux, point the browser's automatic proxy setting to the printed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/proxy.pac` URL and reload proxy settings after joining or leaving a pen. For CLI tools, see [Browsers and command-line tools](https://work.hogman.network/docs/join.html#side).

### "This computer cannot find the network's names yet"

Run the same join command again. The invite already enrolled this workstation, so the rerun skips invite redemption and finishes verifying the portal. (That invite will not work on a second computer — use *Add a device* instead.)

### The setup tool tried to open a browser on a headless bridge server

Pass `--no-open`. The portal URL is still printed to the terminal.

### "is already being shared from this computer"

That bridge is already running in the background or another terminal. Inspect active bridges with `~/hogman-join share list` and stop one with `~/hogman-join share stop NAME`.

### A bridged dashboard says "the app isn't answering right now"

The Hogman bridge node is up, but the local controller or web app is unreachable at the configured LAN address or port. Verify the equipment is powered on and reachable from the bridge machine (for example, `curl -I http://192.168.1.40`) and reload.

### "the invite was not accepted"

Member invites work once and expire after 7 days; personal device links and server share links expire after 1 hour. Issue a fresh link from the portal.

### A workstation ran `leave` and needs access again

`leave` removes the device, not the person's membership. Generate a 1-hour device link from another enrolled device (or ask an owner/admin for a fresh invite if no devices remain) and rejoin.

### "this link is from an older release (carries fp=)"

Links from early private-CA test builds (before public certificates) are rejected. Issue a fresh link; pre-switchover `.hogman` pens must be recreated.

Still stuck? Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/celtiberi/hogman/issues) with the command you ran and the exact output.
